speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; since you are presenting with sudden-onset vertigo, I need to understand exactly what you are feeling. Can you describe the nature of the spinning sensation and tell me if it started while you were still, moving, or sleeping? Also, do you experience any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or nausea alongside this dizziness?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

The duration of your symptoms lasting only 3 minutes and occurring while you were going to bed is highly characteristic of BPPV. Given your age and the lack of auditory symptoms like ringing or hearing loss, this seems to be the most likely cause. Would you like me to proceed with a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm this, or do you have any questions about this condition?
